title: Rigveda 9.104: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.104: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.104 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 734r-734v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.text: <sup>1</sup>SIT down, O friends, and sing aloud to him who purifies himself: Deck him for glory, like a child, with holy rites.

translation.original_ref: RV 9.104.2-6 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 5, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 734v
translation.original_text:
2sam ī̍ va̱tsaṁ na mā̱tṛbhi̍ḥ sṛ̱jatā̍ gaya̱sādha̍nam | de̱vā̱vya1̱̍m mada̍m a̱bhi dviśa̍vasam ||
3pu̱nātā̍ dakṣa̱sādha̍na̱ṁ yathā̱ śardhā̍ya vī̱taye̍ | yathā̍ mi̱trāya̱ varu̍ṇāya̱ śaṁta̍maḥ ||
4a̱smabhya̍ṁ tvā vasu̱vida̍m a̱bhi vāṇī̍r anūṣata | gobhi̍ṣ ṭe̱ varṇa̍m a̱bhi vā̍sayāmasi ||
5sa no̍ madānām pata̱ indo̍ de̱vapsa̍rā asi | sakhe̍va̱ sakhye̍ gātu̱vitta̍mo bhava ||
6sane̍mi kṛ̱dhy a1̱̍smad ā ra̱kṣasa̱ṁ kaṁ ci̍d a̱triṇa̍m | apāde̍vaṁ dva̱yum aṁho̍ yuyodhi naḥ ||
translation.text:
2Unite him bringing household wealth, even as a calf, with mother kine, Him who hath double strength, the God, delighting juice.
3Purify him who gives us power, that he, most Blessed One, may be A banquet for the Troop, Mitra, and Varuṇa.
4Voices have sung aloud to thee as finderout of wealth for us: We clothe the hue thou wearest with a robe of milk.
5Thou, Indu, art the food of Gods, O Sovran of all gladdening drinks: As Friend for friend, be thou best finder of success.
6Drive utterly away from us each demon, each voracious fiend, The godless and the false: keep sorrow far away.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 734v (numbered 51v by the scribe) (OPenn image 735, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.104.2 ‹-mātṛ-bhiḥ sṛjata gaya-sādhanam deva-avyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 735r (numbered 52r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.105.5 ‹saḥ naḥ harīṇām pate›. Verses 9.104.2-6 end on this page; 9.104.2 begins on fol. 734r (numbered 51r by the scribe).
